author: Fixture Reporter
content:
A competing account says Nvidia received exclusive rights to the inference technology covered by its December agreement with Groq. It disputes the original account's description of those same rights as nonexclusive.

The disagreement concerns the license as signed in December, covering the same technology and contractual scope. The competing account does not describe a later amendment or a separate license.

The Justice Department's inquiry into whether the arrangement avoided regulatory review remains underway. Jonathan Ross and Sunny Madra subsequently joined Nvidia, as described in the earlier report.
headline: Competing Account Says Nvidia's December Groq Technology License Was Exclusive
summary: A competing account disputes the original description of the Groq license, saying the same December agreement granted exclusive technology access.
